allGuides.title: The 50/30/20 Student Rule Blueprint
allGuides.description: A balanced, guilt-free framework that divides your monthly income between essential living bills, campus social fun, and future security.
actionItems: Dedicate 50% strictly to rent, groceries, transit, and course materials.
Reserve 30% for campus dining, concerts, and guilt-free leisure.
Lock 20% into savings or paying down student loan balances.

allGuides.title: Zero-Based Campus Budgeting
allGuides.description: Give every single dollar an exact destination before the month begins so spare cash doesn't disappear into untracked convenience buys.
actionItems: Calculate your total monthly income or allowance on the 1st of each month.
Allocate every dollar across categories until Income minus Expenses equals Zero.
Sweep any surplus change directly into your emergency reserve.

allGuides.title: Emergency Fund Starter Cushion
allGuides.description: A modest starter cushion converts an unexpected crisis—like a broken laptop charger or clinic prescription—into a minor inconvenience.
actionItems: Target an initial starter buffer of $250 to $500 while in college.
Keep it in a separate, fee-free high-yield student savings account.
Automate a $10 transfer each Friday right after your classes wrap up.

allGuides.title: The 30-Day Student Savings Sprint
allGuides.description: Build saving momentum with incremental micro-deposits that turn loose change into hundreds of dollars without feeling restrictive.
actionItems: Save $1 on Day 1, $2 on Day 2, up through $30 on Day 30 to accumulate $465.
Reward milestones with free campus events instead of costly spending sprees.
Keep the sum locked specifically for end-of-semester course supplies.

allGuides.title: The Subscription Trap & Zombie Trials
allGuides.description: Forgotten memberships and recurring free trials quietly bleed college student bank cards without providing ongoing value.
actionItems: Always set a calendar reminder 24 hours BEFORE free trials auto-renew.
Rotate streaming platforms: keep only 1 active subscription at a time.
Claim up to 50% discount using your verified .edu student email.

allGuides.title: Food Delivery Fees & Sneaky Surcharges
allGuides.description: Late-night food delivery apps quietly inflate a simple $12 campus meal into a $28 expense through delivery fees, service charges, and tips.
actionItems: Limit third-party food delivery apps to twice a month as a planned treat.
Batch cook 15-minute dorm staples (rice bowls, pasta, wraps) in advance.
Walk to campus dining halls or local eateries for pickup to dodge fees.

allGuides.title: Compound Growth & Broad Index Funds 101
allGuides.description: Time in the market beats timing the market. Investing modest amounts in low-cost, diversified index funds harnesses exponential compounding.
actionItems: Harness the Rule of 72: divide 72 by interest rate to find doubling years.
Focus on low-cost diversified funds rather than risky meme stocks.
Even $25 to $50 a month started in college compounds significantly by age 30.

allGuides.title: Student Roth IRA & Tax-Free Growth
allGuides.description: If you earn taxable wages from campus work-study or internships, a Roth IRA lets your long-term capital gains grow 100% tax-free forever.
actionItems: Fund your Roth IRA using summer job or part-time campus earnings.
Contributions (the money you put in) can be withdrawn anytime penalty-free.
Set automatic monthly transfers of $20–$50 to establish lifelong investing discipline.
